title: Bicycle without wheels
body:
I am playing basketball at a neighborhood court.
Kids all around,
some playing tag,
others basketball, football,

a little boy with his dad trying to learn to ride a bike without training wheels.

He comes right in front of me and stops,
just before I shoot a successful free throw,
he raises his head as if looking at a giant
and tells me, with boundless spontaneity:
-Sir? Do you play for the National Team?
-(laughing) No.
-Ah, because you're really good!!
-Thank you! I used to play for a team in the past.
-Which team?
-In Crete, it's...
-Ahhhhh bravo, I like that team very much!

and he sets the bike in motion.

Children possess kindness. They don't care to know about degrees, distinctions, statistics, and unnecessary fanfare. They don't ask for anything in return to say a kind word.
They won't ask something they aren't interested in;
they won't continue a conversation just because "it's uncomfortable not to speak when you're with someone."

Because children are authentic!
(and cheeky)

y.f.
